title: P2 — preflight silently demotes a ≥0.85 probability to REVIEW via the evidence floor and the console reason misreports why: 0.97 → dispatch-with-note with reason 'the evidence partially resolves the row' on evidence with nothing partial, and no user-facing doc names the floor
detail:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-23 (tick gitreins-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-02-55; scratch consumer repo, wheel-equivalent HEAD 156c36c v0.17.0). The v0.15 defect POC-37 (dual shape) and POC-36 (no persistence) are FIXED and re-verified; this is a NEW UX/trust gap on the same surface.

MEASURED: same question, same repo, seconds apart:
  gitreins resolve "Does summarize.py handle a log line whose level is TRACE?" → RESOLVED (0.97), exit 0
  gitreins preflight --surface cli <same> → decision dispatch-with-note, band REVIEW, probability 0.97, reason: 'the evidence partially resolves the row — dispatch and carry missing_kind + probability into the worker brief'
Mechanism (engine/preflight.py:84-91 calls engine/resolution.py:1530 effective_band_for): the repo has NO tests, so Jev's evidence rubric returns evidence_quality=2 of 4 (legend: '2 = the exact code path is present', '3 = …together with its test'); MIN_RESOLVED_EVIDENCE_QUALITY=3 at engine/resolution.py:182 demotes the band to REVIEW. Nothing in the consumer-facing output names the floor: docs/cli-reference.md §16's table says only 'RESOLVED (probability ≥ 0.85) → skip-dispatch', and spec docs/jev-resolution-gate.md §9 line 105 mentions the floor once in a table cell the CLI user never sees. The printout REASON ('the evidence partially resolves the row') asserts a partial-evidence state that did not occur — evidence_quality was 2 (exact code present), probability 0.97.

WHY IT MATTERS: a foreman consuming preflight --json sees band=REVIEW/probability=0.97 for a row whose answer is in the repo (proven by resolve=RESOLVED on the same bytes), cannot tell WHY it was demoted, and the doc table contradicts the observed behavior. A user tuning resolved_at in config reads the §9 table, sets 0.85, and still never sees skip-dispatch without test coverage — the two surfaces give contradictory verdicts on the same question with no explanation on either.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) when effective_band_for demotes, carry the cause into the record: abstain_detail/notes field like 'evidence_quality 2 < floor 3 (add a test exercising this path to allow skip-dispatch)'; (2) make the printed reason state the actual trigger instead of the generic 'partially' line; (3) one sentence in docs/cli-reference.md §16 pointing at the floor with the legend scale. Evidence: /home/kara/scratch/gitreins-df-20261023/consumer/.gitreins/history/2026-10-23/f445526b/verdict.json (RESOLVED record with evidence_quality 2) and /tmp/df-pf2.json (preflight record). Board context: JEVRES-001/002/003 closed 2026-09-20 era; this gap appeared with the floor added post-POC-37.

title: P3 — resolve's empty-bundle ABSTAIN hint tells a user to 'check that hilo is installed' when the real cause is a missing hilo project bootstrap (`hilo init` + graph cache) — the actionable fix is never named and the hint's URL is wrong
detail:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-23 (tick gitreins-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-02-55; scratch consumer repo, HEAD 156c36c v0.17.0).

MEASURED: on a brand-new repo with hilo binary on PATH but no hilo project:
  gitreins resolve "<any question>" → ABSTAIN, abstain_reason: empty-bundle,
  abstain_action: 'check that hilo is installed and the question names real code — hilo comes from https://github.com/gethilo/hilo (cargo source build), and the abstain detail names the exact path that was searched'.
  hilo IS installed (/home/kara/.cargo/bin/hilo, 0.4.0). Running the hint's suggested fix (re-check install) changes nothing. The real fix sequence a user discovers by trial: `hilo init` then `hilo graph warm` — after which the same command resolves in 0.56s. Two real friction rounds to find it; the abstain_detail string ('no candidate evidence was assembled') names no path and no fix despite the hint claiming 'the abstain detail names the exact path that was searched'.

ALSO WRONG: 'hilo comes from https://github.com/gethilo/hilo (cargo source build)' — this host's hilo comes from a different source/install; the sentence presents one install path as the universal one (same stale-coaching class as the 2026-09-23c finding).

WHY IT MATTERS: a new consumer's FIRST question fails, the fix hint sends them hunting a binary they already have, and nothing on the failure path mentions the two commands that unblock. This is the same 'surface fails closed with an unusable hint' family as POC-27 (worktree fleet prerequisite undocumented): the fix is naming the real prerequisite in the hint, not changing behavior.

FIX DIRECTION: when hilo is on PATH but no graph/manifest exists in the workdir, abstain_reason 'hilo-not-initialized' with abstain_action 'run: hilo init && hilo graph warm' (exact commands). Keep the not-installed branch for a genuinely missing binary. Evidence: /tmp/df-resolve1.txt (before) vs /tmp/df-resolve3.txt (after init+warm).

title: P3 — push-check misses a credential whose literal is split across a string concatenation: 'ghp_' + '<40-char body>' on one line publishes to the remote with PUSH SECRET CHECK: clean, while the same joined literal is refused (engine/push_secrets.py:13-20)
detail:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-23 (tick gitreins-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-02-55; A/B on scratch branches in /tmp/df-ab/upstream, single-commit ranges, engine/push_secrets.py at HEAD 156c36c v0.17.0).

MEASURED A/B (identical byte content except concatenation splits, one commit per range, base 5a2b027):
  branch ab-concat:  STRIPE_KEY = "sk_live_" + "9f8e…3210" / API_TOKEN = "ghp_" + "XXXX…1234"
    gitreins push-check <concat-tip> 5a2b027 → 'PUSH SECRET CHECK: clean' RC=0 — the push PUBLISHES the token to the remote (verified: the upstream bare repo took the commit).
  branch ab-joined:  same literals joined
    gitreins push-check <joined-tip> 5a2b027 → 'PUSH REFUSED: GitHub personal access token…' (rc 1 on direct invocation).
Mechanism (engine/push_secrets.py): all five token regexes need the CONTIGUOUS body immediately after the prefix on one line; the split form puts a quote+plus+quote between prefix and body, and the credential-assignment class (:19-20, [^\s#]{12,}) stops at the first space, so 'TOKEN = "ghp_" + "…body…"' defeats every class: the assignment match fails ('"ghp_"' = 6 non-space chars) and the token regexes never see a contiguous ghp_ body.

ALSO MEASURED, same probe session (pre-existing scope note, recorded as context not a new defect): the guard's SECRETS lane scans the staged diff (protect --staged), so a secret already COMMITTED is invisible to `guard --full`'s secrets cell (clean on a committed-secret tree) — the working-tree scope (`--scope working-tree`) is the surface that catches it; README/§18 never tell a leaked-commit user that. Push-check is the surface that catches the joined form (verified rc=1 on the joined range) — the gap is only its line-shape blindness.

WHY IT MATTERS: the refusal contract is the last egress gate; a user writing 'prefix + body' style constants (common in rotation/escaping code) gets a clean verdict and the credential lands on the remote — the exact publish push-check exists to prevent, and its clean line actively documents the wrong fact ('nothing outgoing').

FIX DIRECTION: match the pattern against the line with quote/concat glue removed as a SECOND pass (strip the literal sequence ' + ' between quoted chunks before regexing), or pre-normalize added lines by eliding ["']["']\s*\+\s*["']. Control: joined form must stay refused (it is) and a 1-char-per-line assembly must be out of scope/acknowledged (document as limitation). Evidence: /tmp/df-ab-build-branches.py (branch builder), branch ab-concat tip bfd6298 vs ab-joined tip 65c73b9.

title: P4 — guard --full's secrets cell reports clean on a tree with COMMITTED credentials: --full extends lint/tests to the whole tree but the secrets lane still scans the staged diff, and no doc names --scope working-tree as the missing-whole-tree-secrets surface
detail:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-23 (tick gitreins-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-02-55; branch ab-joined in /tmp/df-ab/upstream, single-commit tree with a literal credential, guard 0.17.0).

MEASURED on the committed-secret tree:
  gitreins guard --full  → 'Tier 1 Guards: FAIL (test mode: full, whole tree); ✓ secrets — clean (gitleaks + builtin cross-check)'
  guard --scope working-tree on the SAME tree → '✗ secrets — FAIL (builtin cross-check: 3 findings)'
Mechanism: engine/guard_manager.py:1993 always runs `gitleaks protect --staged` (index-vs-HEAD; '0 commits scanned' when the tree is clean) plus the builtin staged-diff scan — the --full flag extends lint/tests scopes (guard_manager.py:511, CLI help 'Grades the whole tree') but NOT the secrets scope, whose staged diff is empty. A user who committed a secret, then runs the guard's own advertised whole-tree check to 'see if the repo is clean', gets a clean secrets verdict naming both scanners. gitleaks direct on the same tree (detect --no-git) reports 2 leaks, so the tooling CAN see them.

WHY IT MATTERS: 'test mode: full, whole tree' on the console line explicitly claims whole-tree grading; the secrets cell silently keeps a narrower scope, and the one scope that sees the tree (--scope working-tree, README.md:491) is unnamed in any leaked-secret runbook. Same class as POC-42 (Go lanes graded the INDEX under --full): --full means whole tree for some lanes, index for others.

FIX DIRECTION: when --full is set, run the secrets lane with the working-tree scanner set (or emit a scope line: 'secrets — staged-diff scope (use --scope working-tree for whole-tree)'), and add one sentence to README/§18 telling a leaked-commit user which check to run. Evidence: logs guard-20261023T102020.383212Z.log (clean) vs the working-tree run in the same repo.

title: P4 — docs/cli-reference.md §16's band table omits the evidence floor: a reader following §16 alone observes dispatch-with-note at probability 0.97 and has no doc surface linking the demotion to jev-resolution-gate.md §9
detail:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-23 (tick gitreins-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-02-55). Companion doc row to JEVRES-007 (same evidence, doc-slice only).

MEASURED: docs/cli-reference.md §16 (lines ~1145-1160) presents the band→decision table with only probability thresholds; the actual gate (engine/preflight.py:84 via engine/resolution.py:1530) additionally demotes any RESOLVED whose Jev evidence rubric < 3 or whose manifest lacks a ≥0.80 ast_exact/bounded-read entry. Nothing between §16 and the spec's §9 line-105 table cell tells a CLI user the floor exists; the observed behavior (0.97 → dispatch-with-note) contradicts the table as written. Spec docs/jev-resolution-gate.md §9's table mentions 'the evidence floor is met' but does not define the values there either (MIN_RESOLVED_EVIDENCE_QUALITY=3 and the 0.80-with-provenance rule live only in engine/resolution.py:182).

FIX DIRECTION: one row in §16's table ('RESOLVED requires ≥0.85 AND the evidence floor — evidence rubric ≥3 WITH the code's test present; otherwise DISPATCH-WITH-NOTE at the full probability, reason names the floor'), plus the legend values in §9. scripts/check_cli_doc_sync.py must stay green.

title: PERF — resolution gate latency is user-invisible at both scales: resolve 0.57-1.08 s warm on a fresh consumer repo, 2.3-3.2 s at gitreins-repo scale (real questions, all four bands exercised); preflight 0.64-0.66 s; guard 264-283 ms; push-check 126-168 ms — no PERF row warranted beyond this record
detail:
DOGFOOD 2026-10-23 (tick gitreins-dogfood-2026-10-23-10-02-55; coding-hermes-perf law: measure the headline op warm AND cold, one measurement per operation).

MEASURED (home-kara host, 16-core loaded box; hyperfine for repeated verbs, /usr/bin/time for one-shot net ops; HEAD 156c36c v0.17.0):
  guard (5-file consumer repo, staged secrets+lint+tests, allow_skips degraded lanes): 264.4 ms ± 13.0 (n=15), 282.6 ms ± 10.0 (n=10, later config state) — command: hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 15 'gitreins guard'.
  push-check (clean 3-commit range): 126.6 ms ± 15.0 (n=15); 167.5 ms ± 10.8 (n=20, 2-commit range to base).
  resolve consumer scale (1 source file, 941-token bundle): WARM 0.57-1.08 s wall across 3 runs (network-dominated: /usr/bin/time -f '%es'). COLD tree (git archive, no .vfs): ABSTAIN-fast 0.195 s (empty bundle), with cache copied 0.561 s — the cold path does not hang on graph build, it refuses fast (see DF-025 for the UX gap that creates).
  resolve at gitreins-repo scale (~2.6k files, gitreins repo itself, cli surface enabled): 2.26-3.23 s wall across 5 real questions incl. RESOLVED 0.92 / REVIEW 0.73-0.78 / UNRESOLVED 0.39-0.46 bands; commands: /usr/bin/time -f 'resolve@repo-scale: %es wall' gitreins resolve "<q>".
  preflight warm: 0.64/0.66/0.66 s (n=3, same question).

VERDICT: nothing here is slow enough that a user would notice — the gate's promise ('~$0.0003 typed decision') also holds on cost (usage.jsonl: 941 in / 96 out tokens, cost_usd 3.9522e-05). No profiling justified; this row is the record that the numbers exist and are healthy. The stage decomposition: resolve wall = hilo bundle assembly (<0.2 s of the total) + Jev API round-trip (dominant, unavoidable). Evidence: /tmp/df-pf-times, /tmp/df-big*-time.txt; usage row .gitreins/usage.jsonl.
